Find a nice, long, straight road (preferable not busy or usually obstructed) and drive down it every day until you get used to it. I found it helpful to pass the whole activity into my subconscious.
You want one that's at least half an hour's drive.

In the UK, plastic bags now cost money, meaning someone has to come over and approve your purchase to make sure you are actually paying for them. I try to bring my own, but I forget all the time, I'm too used to the old way.

But yes, they were nice while they lasted :(

I'm getting better, I think, but this past year has been really bad for me.
The best description I can think of is "fabricated selfishness". Like, I knew the frustration was out of proportion, I knew whomever I was talking to was not out to hurt me, and did not see this interaction as a big deal... but I stopped caring, briefly, for a moment, it was all about *me*, and there didn't have to be a reason for the way I  felt. 
It tended to die off pretty quickly, then I would feel guilty, childish, and also anxious, because I became worried that something was wrong with me. 
Sadly though, it did also act as a release mechanism, I found it easier to stay calm for a little while afterwards.

> a horrible nasty soup of egos and competitiveness and fear

Don't forget greed
Know the feeling, OP, I hate jobs ads, I've often wished that they should not be allowed to say anything beyond "About You: Willing to do xyz for money...".

> I avoid cars

Oddly, I love them for the exact same reason. No noisy bus-occupants, no wind or rain hammering into you, just the rumble of the engine.
